definitions.gloss: Shinto priest; Shinto clergy; shrine priest
definitions.explanation: A person who serves at a Shinto shrine and performs religious ceremonies, rituals, and other duties. The general term for all ranks of Shinto priesthood.

examples.japanese: {神職|しんしょく}が{祝詞|のりと}を{奏上|そうじょう}した。
examples.english: The Shinto priest recited the ritual prayer.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{地元|じもと}の{神社|じんじゃ}で{神職|しんしょく}を{務|つと}めている。
examples.english: He serves as a Shinto priest at the local shrine.

examples.japanese: {神職|しんしょく}になるには{大学|だいがく}で{神道|しんとう}を{学|まな}ぶのが{一般的|いっぱんてき}だ。
examples.english: To become a Shinto priest, it is common to study Shinto at university.

notes:
A compound of {神|しん} (god, divine) + {職|しょく} (occupation, profession). The general term for Shinto religious professionals at any rank.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神職|しんしょく}を{務|つと}める: to serve as a Shinto priest
- {神職|しんしょく}に{就|つ}く: to take up the Shinto priesthood
- {神職|しんしょく}の{資格|しかく}: qualification as a Shinto priest

SHINTO PRIESTHOOD RANKS:
- {宮司|ぐうじ}: chief priest — the head priest of a shrine
- {禰宜|ねぎ}: senior priest — second in rank
- {権禰宜|ごんねぎ}: associate priest — a junior priest
- {巫女|みこ}: shrine maiden — a young woman who assists with shrine duties (not technically a {神職|しんしょく})

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {僧侶|そうりょ}: Buddhist monk/priest — the equivalent for Buddhism
- {宮司|ぐうじ}: chief priest — specifically the head of a shrine
- {神主|かんぬし}: shrine priest — a more colloquial term, often used interchangeably with {神職|しんしょく}
